verdicts.subject: packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen
verdicts.reasoning: The seven-way direction is right and repo-confirmed (five lifecycles, generated output in three committed forms beside hand-written src/bulk and src/synonyms), and nothing proposed is hollow: oak-curriculum-synonyms earns standalone status (editorial lifecycle, two distinct consumer surfaces — ingest-time synonym sets and runtime phrase vocabulary), the vocab-mining/corpus-data pair enacts the owner-named bulk-processing and generated-separation dimensions, and keeping docs-gen and the sitemap scanner as riders is correct. But the set falls short of the owner's named separations in two places. (1) openapi parsing vs type/constant generation: the proposed openapi-pipeline lumps both, and its movesFrom actually scatters the parsing stage — it takes schema-validator.ts but omits schema-separation-core.ts, schema-cache.ts, and resolve-schema-source.ts (verified in code-generation/), leaving spec acquisition/separation homeless in the residue while its cache moves to oak-api-artifacts. The parsing stage is a real capability boundary by the analysis's own transformation 1: its output api-schema-sdk.json is consumed by four downstream generators plus the CI drift check, and it refreshes on upstream-deploy cadence while generator code changes on Oak's generation-design cadence. (2) Generated-separation is applied inconsistently: oak-search-index-contracts bundles hand-written field-definitions/ and generators WITH generated src/types/generated/search/ (15 files + es-mappings/, verified), and oak-bulk-ingest bundles the hand-written reader/extractors/templates WITH generated src/types/generated/bulk/ — both recreate exactly the mixing the same proposal removes via oak-api-artifacts and oak-curriculum-corpus-data. The owner's rule has no carve-out for 'the generator lives next door'. The amendments below cure both; the analysis's caution (1) survives — the generated search requests import KEY_STAGES/SUBJECTS from ../api-schema/path-parameters.js (verified at generate-search-requests.ts lines 20/63/91), so the search-artifacts workspace declares a dependency on oak-api-artifacts instead of using a relative path. The two-file thinness of the bulk artifacts workspace is acceptable because generated-only workspaces are dumb artifact holders, not capability claims; test-cache/ stays as e2e fixture data colocated with its only consumer.

amendedSplits.scope: The spec acquisition and separation stage as its own capability: schema fetch/refresh resolution, committed-cache handling, schema separation and decoration hooks, schema validation, and deferred-path exclusion — parameterised by a config object (decorators, exclusions) so Oak knowledge stays behind as configuration. Its single output is the decorated api-schema-sdk.json artifact that every downstream generator and the CI drift check consume.

Verified first-hand in packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen/src: (1) api-schema.ts is the OpenAPI-derived surface (types, path parameters, request/response validation, schema base) on the upstream-spec clock; (2) src/bulk/ is bulk data processing — extractors plus generators (graph-corpus-*, analysis-report-generator) emitting vocab/graph-corpus artefacts 'produced by the vocab-gen pipeline from bulk download data' — on the bulk-download clock; (3) mcp-tools.ts is the tool descriptor/constant generation surface (MCP_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS, toolNames) consumed at runtime by oak-curriculum-sdk's registry and thence the MCP server; (4) src/generated/vocab/** is TRACKED generated output (data.json + types.ts files, confirmed via git ls-files) committed inside src/ beside handwritten code — exactly the banned shape; (5) Oak-specific surfaces (vocab, synonyms, widget-constants) sit beside the chain machinery. The two-clocks fact is already institutionalised by the estate itself: separate skills exist for the two lifecycles (oak-update-upstream-api-spec vs oak-update-bulk-download-schema), yet both clocks tick inside one workspace. This is precisely the different-clocks merge that makes the owner's separation list binding here, in contrast to the CLI's oak-bulk-data where acquisition and emission share one freshness event. The reusable half of the openapi machinery already has a home (packages/core/openapi-zod-client-adapter), so the amendment is a lifecycle decomposition, not a new genericisation exercise.

verdicts.subject: packages/design/oak-design-tokens
verdicts.reasoning: Both proposals fail against ratified structure. (1) The terminal-theme absorb into oak-design-ink inverts ADR-213's ratified end state: 'the design system owns web CSS delivery, and oak-design-tokens shrinks to the terminal-theme projection', with the ratified dependency edge 'oak-design-ink depends on oak-design-tokens only'. Stage B 'regenerates index.css and the terminal theme' inside this package's build — the terminal theme is a second codegen projection of the same token data, the same lifecycle as the CSS leg (dist/index.css is equally consumed at runtime by browsers; the 'three lifecycles' framing is overstated). Mechanically (verified): terminal-theme.ts imports ./tokens/*.json directly (lines 13-16) and the exports map deliberately exposes no raw token JSON, so the absorb would either mint a raw-data export contract or reach across the workspace boundary into sibling src — recreating the exact cross-package reach the conformance split exists to remove — to benefit a package with zero consumers (verified: no importer of oak-design-ink repo-wide). Consolidate-at-second-consumer cuts against the move, and the change would require an ADR-213 amendment, not a survey-driven reshuffle. (2) The design-system-conformance split has the right instinct but the wrong scope: it moves design-system-contrast.ts (+ expectations, gate-error) out of build.ts, contradicting ADR-213 §2 amendment 2026-07-20, which ratifies the four-theme gate INSIDE this build — 'a studio sync that breaks the four-theme gate reddens the estate build over a source nothing ships from — that early-warning coupling is the point of the wiring, not an accident' — and at Stage B the build re-points its generation at the dtcg export, making that gate this build's own input gate; moved out now, it moves back at Stage B. The analysis's claimed benefit 'removes oak-design-tokens' devDependency on @oaknational/oak-design-system' is false while the contrast gate stays. The amended split keeps the durable, genuinely lint-lifecycle piece only: the dtcg-vs-CSS consistency suite, whose one consumer is repo-validators:check (verified at root package.json), which cannot move into oak-design-system itself (ADR-213: that workspace 'never imports other design workspaces', and the suite imports design-tokens-core and @oaknational/result — verified in scripts/validate-design-system-consistency.ts).

The four-theme dtcg contrast gate (design-system-contrast.ts, design-system-expectations.ts, design-system-gate-error.ts) stays in oak-design-tokens' build per ADR-213 §2 amendment 2026-07-20 (the early-warning coupling is ratified as deliberate, and Stage B makes it the build's input gate). verdicts.subject: packages/design/oak-design-system
verdicts.reasoning: Both proposed splits survive challenge on verified evidence. Studio-capture: 467 of 654 tracked files (71%, verified via git ls-files) are byte-preserved studio output that production code must never import, currently fenced by vigilance (README fence, Sonar scope exclusion, gitignore re-includes); a workspace boundary converts that vigilance to structure, with one lifecycle (byte-preserved ingest) and one sanctioned consumer story (showcase fidelity diff target + studio re-shipping). Theme-runtime: verified that src/ contains ONLY oak-theme.ts and its two tests, that the tracked generated root oak-theme.js and both tracked demo copies exist (git ls-files), and that this is the estate's only tracked-generated-file class — the split dissolves it into ordinary dist consumption and lets oak-design-react's hand-maintained OakThemeRuntime type mirror collapse into a type import. The refusal to split dtcg/ from the CSS is also right: dtcg/README.md confirms no in-repo generator exists and changes land as hand-synchronised same-commit edits held equal by the consistency validator — a cross-workspace seam would break that same-commit coupling; the cure is the studio round-trip regenerator, not a workspace. Two corrections that do not change the verdict: (a) the claim the theme-runtime split leaves 'NO build step' is false — build:flat (the oak-flat.generated.css concat for DesignSync) remains in package.json; (b) ADR-213 §3 names oak-theme.js as part of this workspace's public surface ('built CSS, the theme-switcher JS (oak-theme.js), plus the generated DTCG export'), so the theme-runtime split must carry the ADR-213 surface amendment in the same change — a ratification cost the proposal should state, not a defect in the seam.

verdicts.subject: agent-tools
verdicts.reasoning: The six-way lifecycle decomposition is broadly right — the structural tells are real (102 scripts confirmed in agent-tools/package.json; `build` chains tsc plus two workflow bundlings; scripts interleave `node dist/...` with `tsx src/...`). But the set fails the frame-challenge at four points. (1) agent-workflow-kit is a hollow wrapper: grep over agent-tools/src shows src/workflow-build/ is imported ONLY by src/corpus-analysis/workflows and src/restatement-audit/workflows — both of which the same proposal moves into corpus-instruments. A workspace whose every consumer lives in one other workspace owns no cross-workspace boundary; it is packaging overhead (package.json, build, version, dependency edge) for zero decoupling. Per the estate's own consolidate-at-second-consumer rule, extract it when a second consuming WORKSPACE exists, not before. (2) typescript-estate is mis-bucketed into agent-session-ops: the analysis's own transformation lists its only consumers as three test:e2e smoke gates, and the repo confirms zero imports from any session-ops module (only smoke-tests/typescript-estate-*.smoke.ts). Putting a 105-file corpus-analysis instrument inside the 'live-seat runtime capability' workspace breaks that workspace's ONE-consumer-story claim and bloats the portable core the split exists to purify. (3) mcp-content-current-source is double-claimed: the repo-validators scope says it 'stays Oak-side but joins this lifecycle seam' while content-projection-generators' movesFrom lists agent-tools/src/mcp-content-current-source/. Worse, either home is wrong: the analysis's own evidence calls it 'the heaviest validator, forcing an MCP-app dependency-graph build at lint time' — its lifecycle is build-graph-coupled Oak content attestation, not fast lint-time verdicts, so leaving it in repo-validators would falsify that workspace's single-lifecycle story on day one. Its own scope prose ('Oak-bound and stay beside the MCP surface they describe') is right; the movesFrom contradicts it. This is also the one oak-vs-reusable violation inside the proposal: content-projection-generators as movesFrom-scoped mixes generic projection machinery with two Oak-bound generators. (4) Three modules appear in no transformation and no split: src/mcp-conformance (18 files, its own CLI, smoke gate, and owner-facing reviewer packs — an audit instrument over the MCP server), src/protocol-conformance (imported at runtime by src/collaboration-state/coordination-home.ts AND by mcp-conformance/runner.ts), and src/protocol-wire (sole importer: src/validators/protocol-wire/validate-protocol-wire-contract.ts). Silence here means the residual Oak leaf silts up with at least four lifecycles (install-time bootstrap, runtime platform adapters, audit-time mcp-conformance, plus strays) — the very disease being cured. On the owner-named codegen chain: openapi parsing, type/constant generation, and bulk data processing live in packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen and packages/core/openapi-zod-client-adapter, already separate workspaces outside this subject — agent-tools contains none of that chain, so no owner-named under-split arises here; the generated-output-vs-handwritten violations the analysis lists (tracked .claude/skills and .agents/skills trees, the AGENTS.md generated region, the cross-workspace write into the MCP app's src/generated) are destination-placement facts a generator-workspace split does not itself cure and must be carried as explicit obligations of whichever workspace owns each generator. Net: five workspaces, not six, with the amended assignments below.

The proposal's central judgment — mint NO new workspace at root — survives challenge, and its one 'split' is honestly a push-down, which is the correct instrument. Verified: the root is a composition shell (turbo.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, ~100 forwarding scripts, licence/identity docs), and a 'root-configs' workspace would be the textbook hollow wrapper — nothing consumes the root as a capability. The push-down targets are the right ones and the ordering argument is the strongest part: turbo.json (504 lines) and knip.config.ts (388 lines) are centralised registries of per-workspace facts, and the agent-tools decomposition this same analysis proposes would add five more workspaces to both registries — pushing the facts down into workspace-level turbo/knip blocks BEFORE the split programme multiplies them fixes the generator, not the merge. eslint.runtime-only.config.mjs relocating to live beside runtime-only-scripts closes a real scatter (confirmed at root). The root debris claim checks out first-hand: 'clerk.thenational.academy_Archive [26-08-06 15-29-33].har', copilot-debug-logs/, vercel_logs/, tmp/, and ds-bundle/ all sit in the root listing beside LICENCE and VISION.md — a scratch-routing convention is a real need, though it is hygiene, not decomposition. CHANGELOG.md and pnpm-lock.yaml at root are tool-managed surfaces in their canonical homes; no generated-separation action is warranted. No amendment: the split set (one push-down, zero minted workspaces) is the simpler shape.

verdicts.subject: runtime-only-scripts
verdicts.reasoning: The empty split set is the right answer, and the proposal's evidence verifies first-hand: the directory holds exactly three files (validate-package-manager-version.mjs, its handwritten .d.mts, README.md) — one script, one lifecycle (pnpm:devPreinstall at ingest-time), zero dependencies, ADR-168-fenced. This is already the target shape the owner is asking every workspace to reach; any split would manufacture boundaries where none exist. The analysis's sharper observation — that the residual complexity is SCATTER, not size — also checks out: its unit test lives across the estate at agent-tools/src/install-version-guard/ (confirmed: that directory contains only validate-package-manager-version.unit.test.ts) and its lint config at root (eslint.runtime-only.config.mjs, confirmed). The optional consolidation (a minimal package.json so the directory owns its own lint and test surfaces while the shipped script itself stays dependency-free) is directionally sound and composes with the root subject's push-down of eslint.runtime-only.config.mjs; it is consolidation toward one owner per concern, not a split, and rightly framed as optional. No amendment.

verdicts.subject: packages/libs/graph-project
